stem:
Xavier has a $5$ by $4$ rectangular grid of small squares. He wants to know whether the total number of small squares is even or odd without multiplying $5 \times 4$.

What can he decide?

options.text: Call the row count $5$ the parity answer, without using both dimensions.
Ignore that one side is even, and treat the parity as unknown until the product is formed.
The total is even, because at least one side length is even.
Say the even-or-odd decision is what creates the $5$ by $4$ grid sizes.

teacher.key_rationale: A rectangular grid has an odd number of small squares only when both side lengths are odd. Here 4 is even, so the total is even without multiplying.
